newsitem.title: USA: FASB says deregulation changes utility accounting.
newsitem.headline: FASB says deregulation changes utility accounting.

text.p: A task force convened by the Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) decided Thursday that utilities do not have to write off newly deregulated assets as long as the investments will be recovered through mandated surcharges on utility bills, a FASB staffer said.
Several states are in the process of shifting from the traditional system of monopoly utilities to one of open competition between electricity suppliers.

The FASB task force said utilities without monopoly service territories cannot continue to use accounting standard No. 71, which allows utilities to record certain regulatory assets and liabilities not recorded under generally accepted accounting principles for nonregulated entities.
Utilities must stop using No. 71 as soon as they know details of their individual transition plans, FASB staffer Julie Erhardt said.
But the FASB task force also decided utilities which have been guaranteed by regulators a cash flow stream to pay for previously regulated assets can leave them on their books, Erhardt said.
"Even though those assets grew up as part of the business that is being deregulated, the utilities can continue to carry them as long as cash flows are regulated," she explained.
Erhardt noted the accounting standards board may be asked to clarify other matters related to electric industry restructuring, but nothing further is scheduled at his stage.
